content.text:
I've rewritten `0.svg`, but could not run automated validation or a render in this session. Here is where things stand.

**What the file was.** A bare 41-byte root element with no `viewBox`, no size, and no child elements. It was valid XML but rendered nothing.

**What I assumed.** With no content to refine and nothing else in the directory, I took the filename as the intent and treated the file as a glyph for the digit zero. If you meant different artwork, tell me and I'll redraw it.

**What the file is now:**

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="24" height="24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" role="img" aria-label="Zero">
  <title>Zero</title>
  <rect x="7" y="3" width="10" height="18" rx="5"/>
</svg>
```

**The improvements:**
- **Scalable geometry.** A 24 by 24 `viewBox` plus intrinsic width and height, so it scales cleanly and has a default size when used standalone.
- **Visible content.** A pill-shaped rounded rectangle with semicircular caps, which is the classic sans-serif zero. The stroke stays inside a 2 unit margin on all sides.
- **Theme-friendly colour.** The stroke uses `currentColor`, so when inlined it inherits the surrounding text colour, and standalone it renders black.
- **Accessibility.** A `role` of image, an `aria-label`, and a `<title>` so screen readers announce "Zero" instead of an unlabeled graphic.

**What I could not verify.** The permission layer in this session has no one to approve prompts, and it blocked every verification command I tried: `xmllint`, a Python XML parse, and a Quick Look render to PNG. I checked well-formedness by inspection only. Every attribute is quoted, both child elements are closed, and there is one root. To confirm on your side:

```sh
xmllint --noout /private/tmp/gndfv/0.svg && open /private/tmp/gndfv/0.svg
```
